Button: One primary action per view; secondary and ghost for the rest.
Navigation to another page. Use a link.
Button sizes: Default 32px in tools; large for forms and marketing.
Button with icon: When the icon clarifies the verb: plus for create, download for export.
Icon button: Dense toolbars and table rows, always with a tooltip.
Primary actions. A word is clearer.
Button states: Loading for async saves, disabled when an action is unavailable.
Disabled without saying why. Explain in a hint.
Button group: Related actions or a small view switch.
Unrelated actions or more than four options.
Toggle button: Formatting and view options that stay on until clicked again.
Badge: A short label or count that needs to be seen at a glance.
Long text, or a table full of them. Use status.
Status: State in dense lists and tables: dot plus word.
Categories that are not a state. Use a tag.
Tag: Metadata and user-applied labels that may be removed.
Showing state. Use status or badge.
Avatar: People, with initials or a photo; squares for organisations.
Avatar group: Showing collaborators in a small space.
More than five names without an overflow count.
Keyboard key: Inside body copy about general typing.
Divider: Separating groups when spacing alone is not enough.
Link: Going somewhere: another page or section.
Triggering an action. Use a button.
Spinner: Short waits on a single element.
Skeleton: Page or table loading where the shape is known.
Field: Wrapping any input with a label, hint and error.
Textarea: Multi-line text such as notes and bios.
Select: Choosing one of 5 to 15 fixed options.
Fewer than 4 options (use radios) or searchable lists (use combobox).
Input group: Units, prefixes and trailing actions glued to an input.
Search: Filtering or finding within a view.
Global navigation. Use the command palette.
Password: Hiding values the user needs to read.
Number stepper: Small integer quantities such as seats.
Large ranges. Type the number or use a slider.
Checkbox: Independent yes/no choices and multi-select lists.
Instant on/off settings. Use a switch.
Radio: One choice from 2 to 5 visible options.
Switch: Choices that need a Save button. Use a checkbox.
Option card: Choosing a plan or mode where each option needs a description.
Segmented control: Switching between 2 to 4 views of the same content.
Slider: Precise input. Pair with a number field.
File upload: Adding documents or images with feedback.
Tag input: Free-form lists such as emails or keywords.
Choosing from a fixed set. Use a multi-select.
Combobox: Searching a long list: people, projects, countries.
Date picker: Choosing a date or range visually.
Known dates such as birthdays. Type them.
Color swatches: Free colour input. Add a hex field.
Form section: Long settings forms split into labelled groups.
Stack and row: Spacing children with a consistent gap.
Bento grid: Dashboards and feature sections with mixed tile sizes.
Data that must be compared row by row.
Page header: Title, description and primary actions at the top of a page.
Repeating inside cards. Use a section header.
Aspect ratio: Keeping media at a fixed ratio.
Density: Letting users trade space for information.
Headings: Structure the page: one h1, then h2 and h3.
Choosing a level by size. Pick by structure.
Text styles: Body, muted and caption for hierarchy.
More than three tones in one block.
Lists: Short related items; check lists for features.
Card: Grouping related content with a clear edge.
Card variants: Interactive for clickable tiles; glow for the one featured item.
Table: Small lists of two fields. Use a list group.
Data table: Large datasets needing search, sort and bulk actions.
Table density: Dense for power users, comfortable for readability.
List group: Short lists of people, files or links.
Many attributes per row. Use a table.
Stat: A headline number with a trend.
More than five metrics in a row.
Progress: Known progress of a task or quota.
Unknown duration. Use indeterminate or a spinner.
Bar chart: Trends over many points. Use a line chart.
Sparkline: A tiny trend beside a number.
Anything that needs axes or exact values.
Donut chart: Proportions of a whole, up to five slices.
Empty state: First-use and no-data screens with one next step.
Timeline: Unordered updates. Use an activity feed.
Tree: Hierarchies such as files and categories.
Kanban board: Data that needs sorting. Use a table.
Diff: Large code changes. Use a real diff view.
Carousel: Critical content that must not be missed.
Feature: Short value statements with an icon.
Alert: Persistent, contextual messages inside a page.
Alert variants: Errors and warnings. Use the tone variants.
Announcement pill: A small link to news above a hero.
More than one at a time.
Toast: Confirming an action that already succeeded.
Messages the user must act on.
Upgrade banner: A soft prompt to a paid feature.
Navbar: Top navigation on marketing and simple sites.
Sidebar: Primary navigation for apps with five or more sections.
Sites with two or three pages.
Steps: Progress through a defined multi-step flow.
Menu: The list inside dropdowns and context menus.
Dialog: Short tasks that need focus and a decision.
Long forms. Use a drawer or page.
Confirm dialog: Destructive actions with a clear consequence.
Drawer: Create, edit and detail flows beside the page.
Tooltip: Essential information. It is not available on touch.
Command palette: Fast search and actions for power users.
The only way to reach a feature.
Context menu: Right-click actions on rows and items.
The only path to an action.
Sign in: Authentication with a clear primary path.
Settings page: Preferences as title, description and control rows.
Filter bar: Compound filters with field, operator and value.
A single simple filter. Use chips.
Notifications: Items that need attention, with unread state.
Profile header: Identity and primary actions for a person.
Onboarding checklist: Guiding new users with visible progress.
API key: Showing a secret with reveal and copy.
Displaying keys in plain text by default.
Usage meter: Plan consumption with a warning threshold.
Precise billing data. Use a table.
Hero: Marketing intro with one clear call to action.
Footer: Links and legal at the end of a page.
Dashboard screen: Starting point: key numbers, trends and recent records.
Task-specific work. Use a list or detail screen.
List screen: Finding, filtering and acting on many records.
A single record. Use the detail screen.
Detail screen: Everything about one record with its actions and history.
Settings screen: Preferences grouped by topic with safe defaults.
Loaders: Short waits with no known length; match size to the space.
Anything over a few seconds with a known length. Use progress.
Typing indicator: Chat and AI replies while content is being produced.
Progress, indeterminate: Uploads or jobs with no measurable progress.
Waits you can measure. Show a percentage.
Status marks: Confirming the result of a finished action once.
Persistent status in tables. Use a badge.
Skeleton card: Loading layouts where the shape is known.
Entrance animations: Content that appears after a user action or load.
Content on every scroll. It becomes noise.
Attention: Shake on invalid input; ping on a new item.
Constant pulsing. It is hard to ignore and tiring.
Stagger: Short lists of up to six items on first appearance.
Long lists. Later items feel slow.
Site header: Top of every marketing page; one primary button.
Inside the product app. Use the sidebar shell.
Logo cloud: Right under the hero when you have recognizable customers.
With no real customers. Use metrics or a quote.
Feature grid: Three to six benefits at one level of importance.
Long lists. Pick the best six.
FAQ: Support articles. Link to the help center.
Call to action: The last section of a page, with a single main ask.
Newsletter sign-up: Before the visitor understands the product.
Not found: Any address that does not exist.
Missing data inside a valid page. Use an empty state.
Server error: Unexpected failures where a retry may help.
Validation errors. Show them next to the field.
Offline: When the connection drops in an app that can queue work.
No access: Signed-out people. Send them to sign in.
Maintenance: Planned downtime with a return time.
Unplanned outages. Use the server error page.
No results: A search or filter that matched nothing.
A list that is empty at first use.
First-use empty: A new account with nothing created yet.
Checkout: Taking a payment with a visible total.
Free sign-ups. Skip the card step.
Order confirmed: The moment after a completed purchase or submit.
Directional entrances: Match the direction to where the content comes from: menus down, drawers from the side.
Many directions on one page. Pick one family.
Overlay motion: Sheets, toasts and anything that appears over the page, with a short exit.
Slow exits. People should not wait for things to leave.
Attention loops: One element that needs notice, like a new message.
More than one looping item on a screen.
Hover and press: Buttons, cards and links, to confirm they are interactive.
Touch-only screens. There is no hover.
Text effects: Status text while something runs, such as Thinking.
Scroll reveal and count up: Landing pages and metric bands, once per element.
App screens with data people check often.
Testimonials: Under the hero or pricing, with real names and roles.
Invented quotes. Use real customers or leave it out.
How it works: Explaining a process in three or four steps.
Feature split: One feature that deserves a story with a product view.
Lists of small features. Use the grid.
Bento features: Showing a mix of features where one leads.
Equal items. Use the feature grid.
Pricing with billing switch: Offering monthly and yearly with a named saving.
Comparison table: Plans with many features to compare.
Team grid: About pages that build trust in the people.
Large companies. Link to a careers page.
Contact form: A way to ask a question without an account.
Support for existing users. Use in-app help.
Blog cards: Surfacing the latest posts on a home page.
Changelog: Telling people what changed and when.
Sign up: The shortest path to a new account.
Verify code: Email or phone verification with a one-time code.
Setup wizard: First-run setup in two to five short steps.
Profile settings: Billing or security. Use their own cards.
Search results: A few items. Use a filter bar.
